financial_health.title: Part A: Financial Health & Balance Sheet Resilience
financial_health.description: Evaluates surplus generation, debt prudence, liquidity buffer, and foundational security.

questions.title: 1. Monthly Savings & Surplus Velocity
questions.description: What percentage of your household net monthly earnings is systematically saved or invested?

options.label: Under 10% (Limited surplus accumulation)
10% to 20% (Moderate disciplined savings)
20% to 35% (Strong systematic velocity)
Above 35% (High surplus capital compounding)

questions.title: 2. Ring-Fenced Emergency Liquidity Moat
questions.description: How many months of essential living expenses are segregated in liquid mutual funds / bank accounts?

options.label: Less than 2 months (High liquidity risk)
2 to 4 months (Emerging liquidity cushion)
5 to 8 months (Prudent liquid moat)
9+ months (Robust multi-season buffer)

questions.title: 3. Debt Servicing & Leverage Headroom
questions.description: What proportion of your monthly income is committed to total loan EMIs / debt obligations?

options.label: Over 50% (High leverage pressure)
35% to 50% (Elevated debt commitment)
15% to 34% (Healthy controlled leverage)
Under 15% or zero debt (Maximal cashflow freedom)

questions.title: 4. Life & Health Insurance Protection Audit
questions.description: Does your family have dedicated pure term life cover and comprehensive medical insurance?

options.label: Minimal or employer corporate group cover only
Basic health policy, but term life is under 5x income
Family floater (₹15L+) & pure term life at 10x-15x income
Comprehensive health + super top-up + 15x+ term cover

questions.title: 5. Asset Class Diversification Quality
questions.description: How is your investable net worth distributed across mutual funds, equities, debt, and liquid assets?

options.label: Heavily concentrated in real estate or single asset
Primarily traditional bank FDs and endowment plans
Balanced mix across Mutual Funds, Equities & Debt
Multi-asset institutional structure with periodic re-balancing

questions.title: 6. Retirement & Longevity Compounding
questions.description: Have you calculated your retirement corpus and mapped active systematic SIP compounding toward it?

options.label: Not started or relying solely on statutory provident fund
Ad-hoc savings without a structured corpus roadmap
Defined corpus target with active monthly SIP investments
Advanced multi-pillar compounding roadmap on track

questions.title: 7. Children Higher Education & Milestone Segregation
questions.description: Are major upcoming lifecycle goals (e.g. child education, marriage) earmarked in dedicated folios?

options.label: No segregated accounts or duration matching
General pooling without timeline de-risking glide paths
Dedicated mutual fund folios mapped to milestone dates
Earmarked portfolios with automated asset de-risking schedules

questions.title: 8. Estate Governance & Account Operational Readiness
questions.description: Are nominations active across all investments, folios, bank accounts, and is estate documentation updated?

options.label: Gaps in nominations and missing document inventory
Basic nominations exist; no consolidated estate review
100% active nominations, verified KYC & documented inventory
Comprehensive family governance with registered estate plan

financial_risk.title: Part B: Risk Capacity & Drawdown Resilience
financial_risk.description: Evaluates volatility tolerance, income shock runway, horizon matching, and drawdown recovery capacity.

questions.title: 9. Inflow Stability & Earnings Concentration
questions.description: How stable and diversified are your primary professional or corporate income streams?

options.label: Cyclical income or single client/customer concentration
Single salary or moderately variable consulting revenues
Stable corporate employment or established firm operations
Multiple uncorrelated cashflow streams & dividend income

questions.title: 10. Drawdown Tolerance & Market Correction Reaction
questions.description: If a macroeconomic downturn caused market-linked assets to decline 20% over 6 months, you would:

options.label: Liquidate immediately to cash to prevent further downside
Pause systematic investments with heightened concern
Stay invested calmly, acknowledging standard market cycles
Deploy additional surplus into equities at discounted valuations

questions.title: 11. Investment Holding Duration & Capital Horizon
questions.description: What is the primary timeline for the core capital deployed in your investment portfolio?

options.label: Under 12 months (Immediate liquidity requirements)
1 to 3 years (Short to medium-term allocation)
4 to 7 years (Medium to long-term compounding)
8+ years or multi-generational legacy wealth creation

questions.title: 12. Discretionary Expense Curtailment Flexibility
questions.description: If household earnings contracted by 25%, how easily could lifestyle expenses be curtailed?

options.label: Fixed commitments dominate; very difficult to cut spending
Modest flexibility; could trim non-essentials with effort
Good flexibility; travel and leisure outlays easily reduced
High expenditure flexibility with substantial lifestyle buffer

questions.title: 13. Dependent Liabilities & Family Financial Support
questions.description: How many non-earning family dependents currently rely on your ongoing cashflow support?

options.label: 4+ dependents with extensive recurring financial needs
2 to 3 dependents with moderate education/medical outlays
1 to 2 dependents with well-planned support reserves
Independent financial unit with zero dependent liability

questions.title: 14. Track Record with Market-Linked Products
questions.description: What is your historical personal investment experience across mutual funds and equities?

options.label: Exclusively fixed deposits, postal schemes, and gold
1 to 3 years primarily in basic mutual fund SIPs
4 to 9 years across varied market and interest rate cycles
10+ years across Mutual Funds, PMS, AIFs and Direct Equities

questions.title: 15. Core Wealth Allocation Mandate
questions.description: Which strategic statement best reflects your mandate for your wealth architecture?

options.label: Capital preservation is paramount; cannot accept nominal loss
Cautious yield generation with low volatility exposure
Balanced wealth compounding beating inflation by 4-6%
Aggressive capital compounding targeting alpha outperformance
